title: Mixing time of the torus shuffle
comment: 52 pages, 8 figures, to appear in Annals of Applied Probability
abstract: In 2009, Morris studied a class of card shuffles that can be reduced to a version of the game three-card Monte on a deck of $n$ cards. In the present paper, we extend the technique and analyze shuffles that can be reduced to what we call 3-Monte shuffles. The main feature of a 3-Monte shuffle is that it uses what we call 3-collisions, which are permutations that are equally likely to be a certain fixed 3-cycle or the identity. We prove a theorem that reduces bounding the mixing time of a 3-Monte shuffle to verifying a condition that involves only triplets of cards. Then we use it to analyze a model of card shuffling we call the torus shuffle, which was introduced by Diaconis in 1988. In the torus shuffle, cards are arranged in an $n$ by $n$ grid. The transition rule is the following. In each step, choose a row or column, uniformly at random, and cyclically rotate it by one unit in a uniform random direction. Diaconis conjectured that the mixing time is ${\rm O}(n^3 \log n)$. We obtain a bound that is within a poly log factor of the conjecture.
